steps.name: Radio
steps.text: ...In response to increasing volcanic activity since 1097, Mayor Herman Doykos initiated the Siesta Free State Relocation Project.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: By early 1099, more than 90% of Siestans are expected to leave the volcanos and beaches for a new life in a nomadic city.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: Just to make it clear, girl, you only paid enough to get you to the next hub. You'll have to find your own way from there.

steps.name: Quiet Girl
steps.text: ...I will.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: You say that, but have you any idea how dangerous the barrens are? It's no place for a kid like you.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: Why are you going to Siesta, anyway? Chasing your favorite band?

steps.name: Quiet Girl
steps.text: Work.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: Going from Columbia to Siesta to look for work? You must've been living under a rock for the last 70 years.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: There was a time when people flocked there to make their fortune. They say you could bend down and pick up some obsidian anywhere on the volcano.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: But Columbia is where opportunities are these days.

steps.name: Quiet Girl
steps.text: I interned at a construction company before I graduated. There was a serious accident just as my internship was about to end, and the company blamed it all on me.

steps.name: Quiet Girl
steps.text: With that on my record, the only job I could find was some tiny demolition operation, where I got Oripathy from the way they misused Originium bomb.

steps.name: Quiet Girl
steps.text: I wanted to stay in the city, but got scammed out of my last savings paying for medical insurance.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: Well, that's tough luck.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Don't let Oripathy stop you from being a pillar of the nation! Join the frontier Pioneers!

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The Pioneers provide an opportunity for every child of Columbia to have a better future...

steps.name: Quiet Girl
steps.text: I thought it was time for a change... my grandfather told me Siesta is a beautiful place.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: I hope you find better luck there.

steps.name: Quiet Girl
steps.text: I think I will.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: I've lost my way♪

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: I've lost the path♪
Static overcomes the easy tune that was playing on the car radio.
The truck slows to a halt on the barrens, as though all life was sucked out of it.

steps.name: Truck Driver
steps.text: What the heck is going on?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: One more dessert of the day, please!

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Of course! Would you like to try a different flavor?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Prices here are nothing like Columbia... it's a tourist town alright.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: All the food looks so nice... the cocktails too...

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: All original. Can't get them anywhere else.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Every cocktail has a story. Like this Nutmeg Beach...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Hey—

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Are those two friends of yours?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Yeah, we're all from Lungmen, and we work for the same company. We get along really well.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: But why do they look like they could break into a fistfight at any time?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Even good friends fight sometimes...

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Didn't expect you to grace us with your presence personally, Commissioner Swire.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: The L.G.D. has annual leave. Got a problem with that?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I know why you're here.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I have to say, I was surprised to see you and your family on the list of bidders for the new plate and shopping district rebuilding project.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: *Cough* *Cough*—

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Mr. Enis! A-Are you ok?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Just got a fright... I mean, I choked on something...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Well, MountainDash Logistics's activities in Siesta are no news to me. You want to set up a logistics hub at this plate because of its location. Where's Eurill?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I'm in charge of this project.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Mountaincomm Trade may be a subsidiary of MountainDash Logistics, but I'm not relying on MountainDash's resources at all.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: This boy born with a silver spoon in his mouth says he doesn't rely on his family's resources. Did you bike here?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: This is no time or place for jokes, Miss Swire.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Very well, we'll talk business.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: This is a project with a lot of potential, a lot of eyes on it, including my own.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: It's fair game so long as MountainDash Logistics doesn't have a formal contract with Siesta.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Then may I ask your plans for the district?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Let's call those a business secret.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Shopping center or ski resort, anything with some economic benefit has a reason to be part of the bidding.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I think I saw some engineered lava hot springs on the way here? That seems pretty interesting. Maybe I should rebuild this whole area as a hot spring resort.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: This is serious. Let's talk seriously.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I know your family is a linchpin of the Lungmen economy, and you've contributed much to the city's development.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: But the project in this area of New Siesta isn't just a commercial venture. It has to take into account the city's long-term development, and the livelihoods of the people here.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I'll ask you to rethink, if you're just in this for fun...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Mr. Bison, sir.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: If you're really confident in your proposal, then all you need to do is to outbid me fair and square. Why did you feel the need to come to me here?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: MountainDash's efforts at establishing a large-scale international trade network are innovative, but innovation entails risk.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Why are your methods more correct than mine, when they both involve business and profit?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: If you insist on continuing this pointless competition... I will play your game.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: And I'm happy to play. We have some time until the official bidding starts. We'll each play our hands until then.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: What are you looking at, Snowsant?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Miss Swire! Something is not right with the route that gentleman took when he drove us here. There's no way this was ten kilometers.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: There are greedy people everywhere... where did you get this map?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I said I wanted to borrow a map to look up some sightseeing routes, and Mr. Enis gave this to me. He says it's a commemorative edition issued for Siesta's relocation.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: And so he charged me some more gold certificates...
The map is creased, with a few barely legible routes on it, and childish scribblings for the sea and volcanoes.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: This map's being handed out for free at the city entrance.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (Look of surprise)

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I'll teach him a lesson, next time I see him.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Hum hum♪

steps.name: Relaxed Customer
steps.text: Enis! You're in a good mood. Swindled another new visitor? Someone's gonna beat you up one of these days.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I wasn't ripping off some poor shmoe. These folks, my friend, were filthy rich.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: She was talking big business with that guy from the trade company, hoping to make god knows how much money. Call it a little deductible on behalf of the citizens of Siesta.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Let's go!

steps.name: Curious Girl
steps.text: Is it this one?

steps.name: Curious Boy
steps.text: No, look at the shape. It has three peaks, the one in the photo only has two.

steps.name: Curious Boy
steps.text: Let's keep looking.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Volcano Watchers? I've seen these plants in my mother's notes.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: There's a Siestan legend about flowers that change color based on volcanic activity. Katia and Magna came looking for it the first time they were here.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: There were reports of massive blooms on the slopes before every recorded volcanic activity on Mount Siesta, a beautiful warning of danger.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Did the flowers go extinct?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: The flowers are just a legend. There's no proof that they ever existed, and this word-of-mouth stuff gives us little to work with.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: It would make sense for Originium activity to affect nearby plants.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Would finding this flower provide another way to prevent volcanic disasters?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Perhaps, but I've never heard of it growing anywhere else.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: That's the way Siesta is. There are many legends here; who knows how many were made up just to attract tourists.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Pink clouds on a sunny day, white cliffs by the mouth of a volcano... many people come seeking these legendary sights every year.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I remember you met my parents in Siesta, Professor Keller?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: ...Yes, I did.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: They said they came to Siesta to survey the volcanoes, and ran into a geology student writing her thesis in one of the cafes.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: So they brought her with them when they climbed the volcano.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: I didn't specialize in volcanoes at the time... it was my first time climbing that one. A beautiful sight, it delayed my thesis.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mutti and Vati were always reminiscing about that time.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I want to hear more stories about them. Can you tell me more?
The scholar gazes away, towards the stack of documents in her hand. The air of recollection is quickly diluted by the labors of reality.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Now is not the time to chat. Let's focus on our work.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Professor Keller.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Is the city council meeting over?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: There is increasing public opposition to moving away from the current beachfront. The city council is keen to have an accurate estimation of when the volcano will erupt, and wants us to provide a guarantee for the estimate that we gave.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I rejected it on the spot as being impossible and irresponsible. We try to give an estimate that is as accurate as possible, but scientific survey cannot be held responsible for the government's opinion polls.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Thank you for taking care of that, Dr. Kahn.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: No need to thank me. The volcano museum is your project, and I promised to help so you could focus on more important things.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: This is something that matters to all volcanologists, and I hope—

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: ...Adele?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Kahn!

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: I forgot. Of course you knew each other.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: ...Of course.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Is she here at your behest?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: The museum's collection includes Mr. and Mrs. Naumann's research, and the eruption of Mount Siesta is a rare opportunity. I wanted to respect Adele's wishes...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I just didn't think it was the kind of work that needed to recruit a sickly... someone who's not in the best of health.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I came to help out while on vacation. It's not really a bother...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Kahn has a point. Your health is important. You have to take it easy, Adele.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Let's call it a day. May I ask you to bring Adele back to her accommodations, Dr. Kahn?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: ...Of course.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Have a cocktail on me! Reward for fetching a rare new customer.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: You just wanted someone to test it for poison...

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: I call it 'Cotton Sunset'. How is it?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: It has a... er... 'unique' flavor.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: You're one tough customer.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: So, was that girl a friend of yours?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: She... forget it, I haven't got the nerve to befriend her.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Shame.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Truck driver, Messenger, ticket seller, swimming coach... how many jobs are you working?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: It's the high season, after all. Got to seize the opportunity.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: What do you need money for? Got a girl you fancy?

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: I could give you an advance on your wages, if you're running short on pocket money.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I don't—

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Forget it... seeing how business has been these few months, I should feel lucky that I even get my meals. You should be worrying about dorm fees for the little ones.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Hah, this is nothing compared to the stuff I've seen in the past.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Are you going to tell that story about how you led a protest against the local magnate in Kazimierz through rock music, then went on to a career in Siesta's rock n' roll scene, finally settling down here with this bar? Again?

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Good memory on you.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I'm too old for bedtime stories.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Say, there's something I've been meaning to talk to you about.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Business hasn't been great since last year. I heard things have been going well at the engineered lava hot springs. If we...

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Getting funny ideas again, young man?

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Don't get ahead of yourself. I'm still the owner of this place on paper. You haven't taken over yet.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: This is the coolest cocktail bar in Siesta, and it hasn't changed one bit from Old Siesta to New Siesta. I'm not about to abandon it over a few slow months.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: This isn't a short-term thing... city council people have been here a few times. The whole street could be demolished.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Yet you fixed the sign for the folks next door, while you haven't bothered to fix ours, even though it's been broken for days.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Is a sign going to save the shop?

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Stop worrying about troubles that aren't even here yet. Life isn't nearly as bad as you think.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Act your age for once. Leave the worrying to the old folks.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I want to travel a little once the high season is over.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Sure. Columbia? Victoria?

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Or even further away, just like him. See the world, expand your horizons.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: You're too young to be worrying about the little things.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: What I mean is... I could be gone for a while.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: What's this about?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Oh, I had a little bump while moving some stuff. I thought it was nothing.

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Well, the summer is pretty dry this year. You should have more fruits and veggies. Need a recipe from me?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I'm not a kid anymore...

steps.name: Stylish Shopkeeper
steps.text: Then don't make me have to worry about you. Look the part, if you want to be taking care of other people.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Alright, Mom.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Thanks for the escort, Kahn.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I'm sure you have a lot of work to do. I'll be fine the rest of the way.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Sorry, could you speak up a little? It's noisy out here and I couldn't quite hear you.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Are you worried about me? Don't be, everyday life isn't much trouble anymore.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I didn't think I would see you in Siesta... are you okay?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Your disease...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Well, the Oripathy getting worse can't be helped... but things are largely under control now.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I have to wear a hearing aid and glasses, but I'm getting used to it. I've also gotten pretty good at lip reading!

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: It's just so unfair... a girl as young as you.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: It's not about fair.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I've seen plenty of Infected at Rhodes Island. Many are even younger than I am. Some are little kids who hardly know what's going on. None of them know when their lives will end.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: At least I have a clear goal, and I'm still strong enough to work towards it. I'm one of the lucky ones.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Has it really been so long since you went to Rhodes Island? How time flies... I heard you're still surveying volcanos in person, and even more frequently these days.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: That's... it's dangerous, Adele.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I've talked to the physicians at Rhodes Island. I know how much time I have left...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: But there's so much still to do... I can't let my parents' research end like this.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: You don't have to be the one to do it. Not in your... condition.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What else can I do, though?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Kahn, I... I miss them...
Poor girl. Do you not suffer enough shackles already?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What? I wouldn't call it shackles...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: What's that you just said, Adele?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I... huh?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Adele... I studied with Dr. Naumann for many years.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: She was my greatest mentor. She brought me out of that little backwater, and took me down the path of science.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: She changed my life. I don't know where I would be without her. I could never repay her kindness.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mutti always said you were her best student.
Kahn pauses, as though to muster courage.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I just can't accept the mysterious circumstances surrounding their deaths.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What do you mean?
The night breeze carries with it the sound of guitar.
Street lamps begin to light up, forming a line that leads to the 'volcano' at the center of the city. Mist rises from hot springs in the distance, laying a veil over the night sky.
Adele rubs her eyes.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: You didn't see your parents the year before they died, did you?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: They were always busy, practically living out of their lab at the university. I wasn't even allowed to visit them.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Did something happen?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: As a scientist, I know how inappropriate it is to operate off a biased conjecture. And yet, I can't help but suspect...
My, my, another one with an obsession.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I don't trust Keller, Adele. Be careful.
I don't understand. Why do humans talk so much about things they have never seen? Why to they pretend to have more wisdom than they possess?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I didn't quite hear what you said... might be a problem with my hearing aid...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Sorry, I got excited. It's been a long time since I last saw you.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: It's late. You should get some rest.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: ...See you.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What was Kahn going to say?
Girl? Girl?
Ahem. Hey, can you hear me?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Is someone calling me?
Hello?
